A1.justification: V2 substantially revises the same attention-behavior-guided KV compression work, renaming SurfaceLogicKV to REAL. Both PDFs are complete and readable, including their appendices, equations, tables and figures.

before.justification: V1 reports SurfaceLogicKV benchmark results and original behavior-component ablations in Tables 1–4 and Appendix H, although some baseline results are attributed to prior work.

after.justification: V2 reports REAL benchmark experiments, ablations, resource measurements and synthetic-needle correlation analyses in Sections 4–5 and Appendices A.5–A.7.

M1.justification: Beyond renaming, v2 replaces v1's top-k/needle-overlap behavior weights with sentence-role-based retrieval, bias and distraction weights. Allocation also changes from the explicit layer/head importance product with a 0.01 layer floor to direct per-head INFsc allocation (v1 Equation 6 and Algorithm 2; v2 Algorithm 1). Recent-window retention and top-k history selection remain.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate 16 LongBench and 11 LongBench v2 subsets. V2 removes the four LooGLE tasks and adds extensive question-agnostic evaluation, where compression occurs without knowing the future question (Section 4.1; Tables 18–19), substantially changing the tested input conditions.

E2.justification: DuoAttention becomes an evaluated comparator in v2's benchmark comparisons. Ada-SKV, included in v1 Appendix Table 9, disappears. SnapKV, PyramidKV, HeadKV-R, HeadKV-R2 and FullKV remain, so the comparator changes are limited.

E3.justification: Attention profiling expands from six lengths of 1,024–6,144 tokens to 30 lengths spanning approximately 1K–30K, retaining 33 insertion depths. LongBench v2 budgets expand from 64–256 to 64–8,192 tokens. V2 also introduces cache-ratio protocols and explicit latency, memory and decoding evaluations; these are substantive experimental-design changes.

E4.justification: V2 revises and broadens component ablations and adds inverted-allocation failure tests, random/mean/max scoring comparisons, beta sensitivity experiments, resource trade-off analyses and synthetic-versus-task-extracted needle correlations. These substantially extend v1's component-removal and head/layer analyses (v2 Sections 4.3–4.5; Appendices A.5–A.6).

E5.justification: V1 provides point results without repeated-run counts or significance testing. V2 introduces ten-run latency/memory reporting, five-iteration profiling/decoding measurements, and Pearson/Spearman correlations with p-values (Tables 5–6 and 12–14; Appendix A.5). Benchmark accuracy tables still lack uncertainty intervals.

E6.justification: Existing results are extensively replaced: LongBench v2 FullKV averages change from 34.47 to 31.24, and the proposed method's 64-token average changes from 23.23 to 12.90 (v1 Table 3; v2 Table 17). V2 adds larger-budget, question-agnostic, resource and correlation results, while removing LooGLE and 123B LongBench result blocks. These are changed result sets, not established same-setting performance gains or losses.

T1.justification: There are localized mathematical revisions to the behavior-weight definitions and allocation equation, including removal of v1's layer-importance multiplier. The harmonic-mean INFsc construction and softmax/top-k selection mathematics remain. Neither version provides formal theorems or proofs.

C1.justification: V1 emphasizes surface memorization, logic construction and joint layer/head allocation. V2 centers its contribution on failure-aware head allocation that suppresses bias and distraction, and adds headline claims of 32-fold cache savings and practical inference efficiency. This substantially changes the contribution's meaning and scope.

C2.justification: V1 interprets distracted/subconscious attention as contributing associative logic and motivates protecting apparently unimportant layers. V2 emphasizes bias/distraction as failure-producing noise, asserts robustness to needle phrasing and labeling heuristics, and interprets new tests as generalization evidence. It also adds an explicit limitation concerning multilingual and cross-lingual applicability.

D1.justification: V2 newly reports code availability and describes forward-pass patching, flattened KV storage, a named CUDA append kernel and dual-RTX 4090 hardware for synthetic profiling. These materially expand implementation and access information. However, v1's explicit per-comparison beta reporting is absent from v2's benchmark tables; the sensitivity discussion does not clearly identify their defaults.

R1.justification: V2 substantially expands related work in Appendix A.2, adding sparse-attention and quantization discussions, including MInference, GPTQ and SmoothQuant. Its positioning against HeadKV and DuoAttention shifts toward their alleged neglect of failure behaviors, replacing v1's emphasis on token/layer/head distinctions and layer-wise critiques.

P1.justification: The narrative is extensively rewritten, with a new title, method terminology and expanded author list. The human-reasoning analogy gives way to success/failure framing; related work moves to the appendix, and Preliminary, Resource Analysis and Limitations sections reorganize the paper substantially.

P2.justification: V2 adopts a two-column layout and substantially redesigns the visual presentation. Main benchmark tables give way to line and radar charts with detailed appendix tables; new behavior traces, ablation, sensitivity and resource displays appear. Retained allocation and score-ranking graphics are redrawn or condensed, while several original displays disappear.

improvement.justification: V2 addresses important gaps through question-agnostic testing, stronger controls, resource measurements and needle-transfer validation. However, its central 32-fold matching claim conflicts with Table 17: REAL scores 20.76 at 128 tokens versus HeadKV-R2's 27.89 at 4,096. Its universal question-agnostic superiority claim also has counterexamples in Table 18. Substantial validation gains therefore coexist with material claim–evidence mismatches, preventing a reliable net quality judgment.
